problem: Purely LLM/VLM-based planning hallucinates and only partially complies with natural-language 'what not to do' constraints (spatial, mathematical, conditional), and classical planners cannot ingest such informal constraints. Symbolic-spec methods (LTL/PDDL) and object-based methods (VoxPoser) cannot express invisible or geometric constraints such as a camera FOV or a heat radius.
motivation: Real navigation needs adherence to operator-specified constraints that sensors cannot perceive (hidden holes, heat zones, camera FOV, conditional rules). Reasoning LLMs are slow and give no guarantees, whereas LLMs are strong at code, so translating constraints into code can keep classical search guarantees (soundness, completeness, optimality).
key_idea: Use an LLM only to translate natural-language constraints into executable Python boolean forbidden-region functions, rejection-sample them into point clouds acting as imaginary obstacles, and let A*/RRT* plan in the pruned space.
insight: Separating constraint translation (LLM) from decision-making (classical search) gives 100% compliance in all four scenarios, including correctly reporting path non-existence, where GPT-4o and o3-mini-high direct path generation get 0-10% in S1, S3 and S4 (S2 is the exception). Model ablation shows a binary behavior: code-capable models (Llama-70B/405B, Granite-34B-Code, GPT o1-pro/o3-mini/4o) work every time, so smaller code LLMs suffice. Only Llama-1B fails. Point count K matters: K=100 misses constraints in S1 and S4 (0% success), while K=1000 already gives 100%.
method: Problem formulation: language constraint l mapped to forbidden region C=phi(l); planning in X'=X\C; a plan is invalid if any state lies in C

Constraint code prompting: single-turn template with System Instruction, Environment Block (parsed Gazebo objects or PointNet/PointRCNN outputs), Constraint Block (description + numeric parameters), fixed Python signature returning True if forbidden

Point-cloud sampling: static objects are sampled from bounding boxes; each LLM constraint function is sampled by rejection within an LLM-generated over-approximating bounding box; K points per object/constraint stored in kd-trees

Constrained planning: A* on 8-connected grid or RRT* in continuous space; a successor is pruned if its nearest kd-tree point lies within robot radius R; the search reports non-existence when the queue empties (A*) or the iteration budget is hit (RRT*)
Execution: waypoints are followed by a low-level local planner (DWA in ROS); works with SLAM pipelines, and the constraint functions are auditable and editable by experts

setting.backbone: Llama-3.1-70B-Instruct (frozen, primary constraint generator); also Llama-3.1-405B, Granite-34B-Code, GPT o1-pro, o3-mini-high, 4o; A*/RRT* planners
setting.observation: no onboard sensors; symbolic scene description parsed from the Gazebo environment file (object bounding boxes / point clouds) plus user text
setting.action_space: path waypoints on an 8-connected grid (A*) or continuous space (RRT*), executed via ROS DWA local planner
setting.privileged: ground-truth object bounding boxes / static point clouds and object coordinates parsed from the simulator file; constraint parameters given in the prompt

numbers.extra: K=1000 points; S1 and S3 are unsolvable tasks (success = reporting non-existence)
numbers.evidence: Table 1: success ratio, runtime, path quality averaged over 10 runs

numbers_note: Custom Gazebo scenarios, not a standard benchmark; the reported metrics are per-scenario success ratio, runtime and path length. Baselines (GPT-4o SR 0/100/0/0; o3-mini-high 0/100/10/10) are not listed as own-method numbers.
results: STPR-A* and STPR-RRT* reach 100% success in all four scenarios (S1-S4) with 12-18 s end-to-end latency, most of it LLM prompting time. Vanilla A*/RRT* score 0% and naive GPT-4o/o3-mini-high VLM planning scores 0-10% except in S2. VoxPoser, given the same simplified setup, only succeeds in S2.
limitations: Evaluated only in simulation on four hand-designed static, deterministic scenarios, with ground-truth object information and no real robot
Prompting dominates latency (12-18 s total; larger models take minutes) and there is no comparison against many other baselines
Constraint correctness depends on the LLM producing the right function; failures are binary per model (1B fails), and sampling density K must be tuned
